title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow

nodes.text: Rectified flow is an ODE model dZt = v(Zt,t)dt that transports between two empirically observed distributions pi0 and pi1 by learning, via a simple least squares regression, a drift that follows the straight-line direction (X1-X0) of linear interpolations as much as possible.
nodes.evidence: The idea of rectified flow is to learn the ODE to follow the straight paths connecting the points drawn from pi0 and pi1 as much as possible.

nodes.text: Rectified flow provides a unified solution to both generative modeling and domain transfer, which prior approaches typically treat separately.
nodes.evidence: providing a unified solution to generative modeling and domain transfer, among various other tasks involving distribution transport.

nodes.text: The training objective is a straightforward nonlinear least squares problem solvable with standard supervised learning, avoiding GAN instability/mode collapse, intractable MLE likelihoods, and the subtle hyperparameter tuning of denoising diffusion models.
nodes.evidence: which avoids the instability issues of GANs, the intractable likelihood of MLE methods, and the subtle hyper-parameter decisions of denoising diffusion models.

nodes.text: The optimal drift is v_X(x,t) = E[X1 - X0 | Xt = x], the expectation of the line directions passing through x at time t, which causalizes/Markovianizes/derandomizes the non-causal linear interpolation process.
nodes.evidence: vX(x,t) = E[X1 - X0 | Xt = x], which is the expectation of the line directions X1 - X0 that pass through x at time t.

nodes.text: Marginal preserving property (Theorem 3.3): the law of the rectified flow Zt equals the law of the linear interpolation Xt at every time t, so (Z0,Z1) is a valid coupling of pi0 and pi1.
nodes.evidence: the marginal law of Zt equals that of Xt at every time t, that is, Law(Zt) = Law(Xt), for all t in [0,1].

nodes.text: Rectification turns an arbitrary coupling into a deterministic coupling with provably non-increasing transport cost simultaneously for all convex cost functions c (Theorem 3.5), giving a Pareto descent without targeting any specific c.
nodes.evidence: The coupling (Z0, Z1) yields lower or equal convex transport costs than the input (X0, X1) ... for any convex cost c

nodes.text: Reflow recursively applies rectification, training new rectified flows on data simulated from the previous flow; this both decreases transport cost and progressively straightens the flow paths.
nodes.evidence: recursively applying rectification allows us to obtain a sequence of flows with increasingly straight paths

nodes.text: Straight paths are preferred because they are the shortest paths between two endpoints and can be simulated exactly without time discretization, so a perfectly straight path requires only a single Euler step and is effectively a one-step model.
nodes.evidence: perfectly straight paths can be simulated exactly with a single Euler step and is effectively a onestep model.

nodes.text: Rectified flow is purely ODE-based and is both conceptually simpler and practically faster at inference than the SDE-based approaches of DDPM, score-based models, and DDIM.
nodes.evidence: Our method is purely ODE-based, and is both conceptually simpler and practically faster in inference time than the SDE-based approaches of [23, 73, 70].

nodes.text: On CIFAR-10 the method achieves state-of-the-art one-step fast diffusion/flow results with FID 4.85 and recall 0.51.
nodes.evidence: we claim a state-of-the-art result of FID (4.85) and recall (0.51) on CIFAR10 for one-step fast diffusion/flow models

nodes.text: The 1-rectified flow yields good image generation with very few (>=2) Euler steps, and after one reflow the 2-rectified flow has nearly straight trajectories giving good results with a single Euler step.
nodes.evidence: the straightened reflow induced from 1-rectified flow (denoted as 2-rectified flow) has nearly straight line trajectories and yield good results even with one discretization step.

nodes.text: Unlike optimal transport methods that explicitly optimize a given cost c, recursive rectification does not guarantee the c-optimal coupling for any specific c, except in the one-dimensional case where the fixed point coincides with the unique monotonic coupling minimizing all convex costs.
nodes.evidence: recursive application of Rectify does not guarantee to attain the c-optimal coupling for any given c, with the exception in the one-dimensional case
